security_audit.summary: The audit found one real medium-risk filesystem issue: scripts/optimize-prompt.py writes optimization results to a caller-provided filename. The remaining static hits are false positives from documentation examples, JSON snippets, Python dictionary key access, and Markdown code fences. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or data exfiltration intent in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict export_results to a configured output directory, reject parent-directory traversal, and warn users not to pass untrusted filenames.
Clarify that documentation snippets are examples only, and avoid ellipsis sequences that resemble filesystem traversal when possible.

content.value_statement: LLM prompts can fail through unclear instructions, weak examples, or missing evaluation. This skill provides templates, reasoning patterns, and optimization workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides few-shot example selection using semantic similarity, diversity, difficulty, and error-based strategies.
Explains chain-of-thought, verification, and self-consistency patterns for complex reasoning tasks.
Provides reusable templates for classification, extraction, generation, transformation, analysis, and question answering.
Describes A/B testing, prompt versioning, and metrics for prompt optimization.
Includes a Python example script for evaluating prompt variants with a mock LLM client.
Shows system prompt structures for roles, constraints, output formats, and test cases.
limitations: The included script uses a mock client and simple text matching by default.
Users must adapt templates to their model, policy, data, and product context.
The skill does not provide live benchmark results or automated safety certification.
Some examples are illustrative and may need production hardening before reuse.

use_cases.title: Plan prompt quality metrics

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to improve a prompt for {task}. Keep the output format simple. Explain the revised prompt and why each change helps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Few-Shot Examples
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design three few-shot examples for {task}. Include typical inputs, edge cases, and the expected output style.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create an evaluation plan for {prompt_name}. Define metrics, test cases, failure categories, and an iteration process.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Prompt System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a production prompt system for {application}. Include system prompt structure, template variables, validation rules, versioning, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Improve a sentiment classification prompt for support tickets.
output_examples.output: A refined instruction, three labeled examples, validation criteria, and notes on ambiguous tickets.

output_examples.input: Create a prompt testing plan for a RAG answer generator.
output_examples.output: A test matrix covering groundedness, citation quality, refusal behavior, latency, and failure tracking.

output_examples.input: Design a system prompt for a data analyst assistant.
output_examples.output: A role definition, supported tasks, constraints, reporting format, and a checklist for validating responses.

best_practices: Start with the simplest prompt that can meet the task, then add examples or reasoning only when tests show a need.
Version prompts and evaluate changes with stable test cases before production use.
Separate role, task, context, examples, and output format so each part can be reviewed.
anti_patterns: Adding long reasoning instructions to simple tasks that need direct answers.
Using examples that do not match the input distribution or expected output style.
Treating prompt templates as safe without testing edge cases, policy limits, and failure modes.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design, test, and refine prompts for LLM applications, agents, and structured generation workflows.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is model-agnostic and includes workflows relevant to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run prompt optimization automatically?
faq.answer: It includes an example Python optimizer, but users must connect a real LLM client for production testing.

faq.question: Is chain-of-thought always recommended?
faq.answer: No. The references recommend reasoning patterns for complex tasks and direct prompts for simple or latency-sensitive tasks.

faq.question: Can this replace safety review?
faq.answer: No. It improves prompt quality, but teams still need product safety, privacy, and abuse testing.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, prompt designers, product teams, and documentation teams can use it to standardize prompt workflows.
